questions.question:
Given `

Hi

` and the rules `p { color: green; }`, `.text { color: blue; }`, `#intro { color: red; }`, what colour is the text?
questions.explication: Specificity decides between matching rules: ID selector (#intro) beats class (.text), which beats type (p). So red wins.
questions.piege: Source order ("last rule wins") only matters when the competing rules have the SAME specificity.

questions.question: According to the course, what is the CSS specificity order from highest to lowest?
questions.explication: Inline styles are the most specific, then ID selectors, then class selectors, then type (tag) selectors.

questions.question: What is a callback function in JavaScript?
choix: A function that keeps calling itself until a condition is met
A function declared as a method inside an object
A function that runs automatically on page load
A function passed as an argument to another function
questions.explication: A callback is passed as an argument (e.g. `sayHello("Alice", farewell)`) and called later by the receiving function.

questions.question:
What does this code print?
`function sayHello(name, cb) { console.log("Hello, " + name); cb(); }`
`function farewell() { console.log("Goodbye!"); }`
`sayHello("Alice", farewell);`
choix: A TypeError: cb is not defined
questions.explication: sayHello first logs the greeting, then calls the callback `cb()`, which is `farewell`.
questions.piege: Passing `farewell` (no parentheses) passes the function itself; `farewell()` would call it immediately.

questions.question: In the CSS box model, what is the order of layers from the inside out?
questions.explication: Content sits in the middle, padding surrounds it, then the border, and margin is the outer space.
questions.piege: Padding is INSIDE the border, margin is OUTSIDE it.

questions.question: Which line correctly links an external stylesheet?
questions.explication: External CSS uses `<link rel="stylesheet" href="...">`. External JS uses `<script src="...">`.

questions.question:
This handler never runs. Why?
`document.getElementById("myBtn").addEventListener("onclick", function() { alert("Hi"); });`
choix: addEventListener only works on links, not buttons
getElementById needs a "#" before the id value
The callback must be a named function, not anonymous
The event name must be "click", not "onclick"
questions.explication: addEventListener takes the event name without the "on" prefix: "click", "mouseover", "keydown", "submit". The "on" prefix is for HTML attributes like `onclick="..."`.
questions.piege: `getElementById("myBtn")` takes the bare id. The "#" is only used in CSS selectors / querySelector.

questions.question: Which of these is an element PROPERTY (rather than an HTML attribute) according to the course?
questions.explication: Attributes (class, id, src, href) are written in the markup. Properties such as innerHTML and value are characteristics accessed through JavaScript.

questions.question:
What is printed?
`console.log('First');`
`setTimeout(() => console.log('Second'), 2000);`
`console.log('Third');`
questions.explication: setTimeout is asynchronous: it schedules 'Second' and lets the next line run right away, so 'Third' prints before 'Second'.
questions.piege: Even `setTimeout(..., 0)` would still print 'Third' before 'Second'.

questions.question: What is a Single-Page Application (SPA)?
choix: An app that loads one HTML page and updates content dynamically
An app where every link reloads a brand-new HTML page from the server
An app made of a single component with no routing at all
An app whose pages are all generated by Pug on the server
questions.explication: An SPA loads a single HTML page once, then JavaScript swaps views without full page reloads.

questions.question: In an SPA built with Vue.js, who handles routing when the user clicks a link?
choix: The database, which picks the matching view
The DNS server, which resolves the new path
The web server, which sends a new HTML file
questions.explication: In SPAs routing is client-side: Vue Router reads the new URL and displays the matching component without reloading the page.
questions.piege: Full page reloads per URL are typical of traditional multi-page applications (MPA).

questions.question: What does React use to render efficiently and avoid re-rendering the entire UI?
questions.explication: React compares a Virtual DOM with the previous one and only updates what changed. Two-way binding and dependency injection are Angular features.

questions.question: Which example illustrates DECLARATIVE programming, as described in the course?
questions.explication: Declarative code describes WHAT you want (SQL query, HTML structure), not HOW to do it step by step. Components also follow this style.

questions.question: In the MVC example with Vue.js, which part is the `updateMessage` method that changes `message` when a button is clicked?
questions.explication:
Model = the `message` data, View = `

{{ message }}

`, Controller = the method that reacts to user input and modifies the model.

questions.question: What is the main difference between HTTP and HTTPS?
choix: HTTPS skips the DNS lookup entirely
HTTPS sends pages without any headers
HTTPS only works with the POST request method
questions.explication: HTTPS is HTTP with authentication and encryption (SSL/TLS certificate). HTTP sends data unencrypted.

questions.question: Which statement about the POST method is TRUE?
choix: The request is cached by the browser
Data is sent in the request body
Data appears in the URL query string
questions.explication: POST puts data in the body, is not cached, does not appear in history, cannot be bookmarked and has no length limit. The other three options describe GET.
questions.piege: Use GET to retrieve data; use POST to create/update data or to send sensitive data.

questions.question: In a Vue instance, what is the role of the `el` option?
choix: It mounts Vue to a DOM element
questions.explication: el = mounting point (e.g. '#app'); data = reactive data; computed = derived state; methods = functions/behaviour.

questions.question: Which option should hold a value derived from other data, e.g. a reversed message?
questions.explication: computed defines reactive, derived state: `reversedMessage()` is recalculated automatically when `message` changes.

questions.question: With `message: 'Hello, Vue!'`, what does `{{ reversedMessage }}` display, given `reversedMessage() { return this.message.split('').reverse().join(''); }`?
questions.explication: split('') makes an array of characters, reverse() reverses it, join('') rebuilds the string: every character, including the comma and space, is reversed.

questions.question: In Vue 2, how do you make a property added dynamically after creation reactive?
questions.explication: Vue 2 (Object.defineProperty) cannot detect new properties, so `Vue.set(this.$data, 'prop', value)` is needed. In Vue 3, `reactive()` (Proxy) handles new properties automatically.
questions.piege: `reactive()` is the Vue 3 answer, not Vue 2.

questions.question: Which mechanism does Vue 3 use behind the scenes to track data changes?
questions.explication: Vue 2 uses getters/setters via Object.defineProperty; Vue 3 uses Proxy, which also detects added properties.

questions.question: Which code correctly creates and mounts a Vue 3 application?
questions.explication: Vue 3: `const { createApp } = Vue; createApp({...}).mount('#app')`. Vue 2 used `new Vue({ el: '#app', ... })` or `.$mount('#app')`.

questions.question:
With `html: 'Hi'`, what does `

` display?
choix: The word Hi rendered in bold type
Nothing, because v-text strips HTML tags
questions.explication: v-text renders plain text, so tags are shown as text. To interpret the HTML you need v-html.
questions.piege: v-html renders raw HTML; v-text and {{ }} do not.

questions.question: Which directive gives two-way data binding on a form input?
questions.explication: `<input v-model="message">` updates `message` as the user types and updates the input when `message` changes. v-bind is one-way only.

questions.question: What is the shorthand for `v-on:click="handleClick"`?
questions.explication: `@` is the shorthand for v-on (events); `:` is the shorthand for v-bind (attributes).

questions.question: What is the shorthand for `v-bind:src="imageSource"`?
questions.explication: `:attr` = v-bind:attr. It binds an attribute dynamically to a data property.

questions.question:
Given `isVisible: false` and `isLoading: true`, what does this render? `
Visible content
` `
Loading...
` `
No data available
`
questions.explication: v-if is false, so Vue tests v-else-if, which is true: only "Loading..." is rendered.

questions.question: Why do we add `:key="item.id"` in `<li v-for="item in items" :key="item.id">`?
choix: To give each item a unique identity for updates
To sort the list in ascending order using the id
To display the id next to the item name
To make the items array editable with v-model
questions.explication: The key lets Vue track each element and update the list efficiently when items are added, removed or reordered.

questions.question: What are Vue.js directives?
choix: Special tokens in markup telling Vue to act on the DOM
CSS classes that Vue applies automatically
Global variables shared by every component in the app
Functions declared in the methods option
questions.explication: Directives (v-if, v-for, v-on, v-bind, v-model...) are special attributes in the template that tell Vue to do something to a DOM element.

questions.question: What are props used for in Vue components?
choix: Sending events from child to parent
Passing data from parent to child
questions.explication: `<my-component :message="parentMessage">` passes data down; the child declares `props: ['message']`.
questions.piege: Child → parent communication uses events (`$emit`), not props.

questions.question: How does a child component send data back to its parent?
questions.explication: The child emits a custom event with a payload; the parent listens with `@updateMessage="updateMessage"`.

questions.question: In Vue 3, to support `v-model` on a custom component, the component must...
choix: declare `v-model` as an entry inside its own `props` array
use `v-bind` on its root element with `sync`
accept the `value` prop and emit the `input` event
questions.explication: Vue 3 default: prop `modelValue` + event `update:modelValue`, e.g. `this.$emit('update:modelValue', event.target.value)`.
questions.piege: `value` + `input` is the Vue 2 convention.

questions.question: In a child component template, what does `<slot></slot>` do?
choix: Reserves space for an async component
Declares a prop received from the parent
Creates a new route for the component
Shows content passed by the parent
questions.explication: Slots distribute content: whatever the parent places between `<my-component>...</my-component>` is rendered where `<slot>` is.

questions.question: How do you register a component globally in Vue 3?
questions.explication: In Vue 3 you call `app.component()` on the app returned by createApp. Vue 2 used `Vue.component()`.

questions.question: What is the purpose of `const AsyncComponent = () => import('./AsyncComponent.vue');`?
choix: Render the component on the server side
Load the component only when needed
Run the component in a separate thread
Fetch the component's data from an API
questions.explication: Async components are lazy-loaded: the code is split and only downloaded when the component is needed, improving performance.

questions.question: In a Single File Component, what does `<style scoped>` do?
choix: Converts the styles into inline style attributes
Loads the styles only after the page loads
Applies the styles to the whole application
Applies the styles to this component only
questions.explication: An SFC (.vue) has three blocks: template, script, style. `scoped` limits the CSS to the current component.

questions.question:
`
A

Note

B
` gives a warning and "B" never behaves as expected. What is the bug?
choix: v-else must directly follow the v-if element
The p element must also have v-if
v-if cannot be used on a div element
v-else needs its own condition, like v-else="!ok"
questions.explication:
v-else (and v-else-if) must immediately follow an element with v-if or v-else-if. The `

` in between breaks the chain.

questions.question:
A Vue 3 component is written as `{ data: { count: 0 }, template: '

{{ count }}

' }` and fails. Why?
choix: The template must use v-text, not {{ }}
`count` must be declared inside the `computed` option
`data` must be a function returning an object
questions.explication: In components (and in Vue 3 apps) `data` must be a function: `data() { return { count: 0 }; }`, so each instance gets its own state.

questions.question: Clicking the button does nothing: `methods: { increment() { count += 1; } }`. What is the fix?
questions.explication: Inside methods, data properties are accessed through `this`. `count` alone is an undefined variable (ReferenceError).

questions.question: `<my-component message="parentMessage"></my-component>` displays the word "parentMessage" instead of its value. Why?
choix: The prop name must be written in capitals
The child must use `$emit` to read the value
questions.explication: Without `:`, the attribute is passed as a literal string. `:message="parentMessage"` evaluates the expression and passes the data value.

questions.question:
The child template uses `{{ message }}` and the parent passes `:message="msg"`, but nothing is shown. The child is `{ template: '
{{ message }}
' }`. What is missing?
questions.explication: The child must declare the props it receives (`props: ['message']`); otherwise `message` is not available in its template.

questions.question: What is the role of `<router-view>` in App.vue?
choix: It creates a clickable link that navigates to another page
It displays the component matching the current URL
It lists every route defined in the router
It reloads the page when the URL changes
questions.explication: `<router-view>` is the placeholder where Vue Router renders the component of the matched route.
questions.piege: Links are created with `<router-link>`, not `<router-view>`.

questions.question: With the route `{ path: '/profile/:id', component: UserProfile }`, how does UserProfile read the id?
questions.explication: `$route` is the current route (params, query...); `$router` is the router object used to navigate.
questions.piege: `req.params.id` is the Express.js (server) equivalent, not Vue.

questions.question: How do you navigate to `/profile/123` from code in a Vue component?
questions.explication: `this.$router.push()` changes the route without reloading the page.

questions.question: Which statement describes Node.js?
choix: A JavaScript runtime outside the browser, built on V8
A database server for storing JSON data
A template engine that uses indentation
A front-end framework for building reusable UI components
questions.explication: Node.js is an open-source, cross-platform runtime built on Chrome's V8 engine. It is single-threaded, event-driven and non-blocking.

questions.question: What does `app.use(express.static('public'));` do?
choix: Makes every route in the app public (no auth)
Starts the server on the 'public' port
Sets 'public' as the folder where Pug views are stored
Serves files like CSS and images from 'public'
questions.explication: express.static is a middleware that serves static assets (images, CSS, JS) from the given folder.
questions.piege: The views folder is set with `app.set('views', './views')`.

questions.question:
Every request hangs after this middleware runs. What is wrong?
`app.use((req, res, next) => { console.log('Request at ' + Date.now()); });`
questions.explication: A middleware must either send a response or call `next()` to pass control on. Without it, the request-response cycle stops.

questions.question: In `app.post('/submit', (req, res) => res.send(req.body.username));`, `req.body` is undefined. What is the likely fix?
choix: Set Pug as the view engine for the app
questions.explication: Form data is only available in req.body after a body parser: `app.use(bodyParser.urlencoded({ extended: true }))` (or `express.urlencoded`).

questions.question: For the route `app.get('/user/:id', ...)`, how do you read the id in Express?
questions.explication: Route parameters are in `req.params`. Form data from POST is in `req.body`.

questions.question: How does Express recognise an error-handling middleware?
choix: It takes four arguments: (err, req, res, next)
It is always declared before every other route in the app
questions.explication: Express treats a middleware with 4 parameters `(err, req, res, next)` as an error handler, e.g. `res.status(500).send('Something went wrong!')`.

questions.question: With `- var name = "John"`, how do you display "Hello, John" in a paragraph?
questions.explication: Pug interpolates with `#{...}`. `{{ }}` is Vue syntax, `${}` is JS template literals, `<%= %>` is EJS.
questions.piege: `h1= message` (with =) outputs the whole value of a variable; `#{}` inserts it inside text.

questions.question: Which Pug code renders one `li` for each element of `items`?
choix: `ul` then indented `v-for item in items` / `li {{ item }}`
`ul` then indented `each item in items` / `li= item`
questions.explication: Pug loops with `each item in items`, and the indentation defines nesting. `li= item` outputs the value.

questions.question: `index.pug` starts with `extends layout`. What must it then define to fill the layout?
choix: A `mixin layout()` with exactly the same name
questions.explication: Template inheritance: layout.pug declares `block content`; index.pug uses `extends layout` and redefines `block content`.

questions.question: Given `mixin greeting(name)` / `p Hello #{name}`, how do you call the mixin?
questions.explication: Mixins are reusable blocks of markup (DRY). They are called with the `+` prefix.

questions.question: Which HTML element is meant to hold a block of navigation links?
questions.explication: `<nav>` is the semantic element for a group of navigation links (menu, table of contents).

questions.question: Which pair of elements shows an image together with its caption?
questions.explication: `<figure>` wraps the image and `<figcaption>` gives its caption.
questions.piege: `<caption>` is the title of a `<table>`, not of an image.

questions.question: Which elements create a collapsible block whose title always stays visible?
questions.explication: `<details>` is a disclosure widget: its `<summary>` is always shown, and clicking it opens or closes the rest of the content.

questions.question: Which element is meant for content only indirectly related to the main content, like a sidebar?
questions.explication: `<aside>` holds content only indirectly related to the main content: a sidebar, related links, extra info.

questions.question: Which element represents a self-contained piece of content, such as a blog post or a product sheet?
questions.explication: `<article>` is an independent unit of content (a post, a product sheet, a news item).

questions.question: Why does the course recommend semantic HTML (header, nav, main, article…)?
choix: It describes the role of each part of the page
It is required for JavaScript events to fire
It replaces the need for the <head> element
It makes the page load without any CSS file
questions.explication: Semantic elements say what each part IS, which helps readability, accessibility and search engines. Using them is one of the best practices listed in the course.

questions.question: Which attribute gives the alternative text of an image?
questions.explication: `alt` describes the image when it cannot be seen (screen readers, broken link). `src` gives the image file.

questions.question: Which CSS declaration hides an element AND removes it from the page layout?
questions.explication: `display: none` hides the element and frees its space. Setting `display: block` (or flex…) shows it again; this is the classic way to build tabs or toggles.

questions.question: Which line makes a hidden element with id `c2` visible again?
questions.explication: JavaScript changes the inline style through `element.style.display`: 'block' shows the element, 'none' hides it.
questions.piege: No `#` inside getElementById.

questions.question: What does `display: flex;` on a container do?
choix: Hides every child except the first one
Turns each child into a clickable button
Makes the container ignore its padding and its margins entirely
Lets its children resize and line up to fill the space
questions.explication: A flex container arranges its items in a row (by default) and can change their width, height and order to fill the available space.

questions.question: Which CSS property shows a hand cursor when the mouse is over a tab?
questions.explication: `cursor: pointer` is the usual signal that an element is clickable.

questions.question:
`
Tab 1
` calls `function tab(t) {...}`. What is `t` when the div is clicked?
questions.explication: The argument written in the call is passed as is: `tab(1)` gives `t = 1`. One function can then serve several elements.

questions.question: What is the difference between `let` and `const`?
choix: `let` creates a variable shared by all pages
`let` can only hold numbers and strings
questions.explication: Both declare block-scoped variables; a `const` cannot be given a new value, a `let` can.
questions.piege: A `const` object can still have its properties changed; only the variable itself cannot be reassigned.

questions.question: What does this print? `for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) { console.log(i); }`
questions.explication: i starts at 0 and the loop runs while i < 3, so it logs 0, 1 and 2.

questions.question: With `let person = { name: 'John', age: 30 };`, how do you read the age?
questions.explication: Object properties are read with dot notation (`person.age`) or brackets (`person['age']`).

questions.question: Two stylesheets set `p { color: blue; }` then `p { color: green; }` (same selector). Which colour applies?
questions.explication: Same specificity → the cascade applies: the rule read last wins.

questions.question: Where should `<link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">` normally go?
questions.explication: Stylesheet links belong in the `<head>`, so styles are known before the body is displayed.

questions.question: Which tool does the course suggest to debug JavaScript?
choix: An HTML validator and the CSS cascade
Reloading the page each time with the browser cache cleared
questions.explication: Log values with `console.log()` and read them, with errors, in the Console tab of the developer tools.

questions.question: With `div { margin: 20px; padding: 10px; border: 1px solid black; }`, which space is INSIDE the border?
questions.explication: Padding sits between the content and the border; margin is outside the border.

questions.question: Which JavaScript event fires when a form is sent?
questions.explication: Common events from the course: click, mouseover, keydown, submit.

questions.question: What does front-end development focus on?
choix: The operating system of the web server
The UI, the UX and performance in the browser
The database schema and server security
The network routers and the DNS configuration of the site
questions.explication: Front-end = everything the user experiences directly in the browser: user interface, user experience and performance.

questions.question: Which description fits Angular?
choix: A small library for adding animations
A state manager designed specifically for React apps
A TypeScript framework for large applications
A template engine based on indentation
questions.explication: Angular is a complete, opinionated TypeScript framework, with MVVM, dependency injection and two-way binding.

questions.question: Why is Vue called a "progressive" framework?
choix: It can be adopted step by step in a project
It loads pages progressively from the top
It updates itself to the newest version
It only works with the latest browsers
questions.explication: Vue emphasises incremental adoption: you can add it to part of an existing page (via a CDN) and grow from there.

questions.question: In React, which line creates a state variable `count` starting at 0?
questions.explication: `useState` returns the value and the function that updates it. `data()` is the Vue equivalent.

questions.question: In Vuex, where do you define the functions allowed to change the shared state?
questions.explication: A Vuex store has a `state` and `mutations` such as `increment(state) { state.count++ }`.
questions.piege: Reducers belong to Redux (React).

questions.question: When do you need a global state manager like Vuex or Redux?
choix: When the app has no routes at all
When a component has only one data property
When several components share the same data
When the page uses only HTML and CSS
questions.explication: Local state lives in one component; global state is for data that several components must read and update.

questions.question: In Angular's MVVM workflow, what does the ViewModel do?
choix: Sends HTTP requests to the DNS server
Replaces the database in small apps
Stores the HTML template and the CSS of each component
Exposes Model data to the View and handles its actions
questions.explication: The View binds to the ViewModel; the ViewModel reads or changes the Model and presents data for the View.

questions.question: What is an advantage of an SPA over a traditional multi-page site?
choix: No JavaScript is needed at all
Each URL downloads a new HTML file
Every page is rebuilt by the server
questions.explication: SPAs load only what is needed and swap views without refreshing the page: faster and smoother.

questions.question: In hash-based routing, which part of the URL changes when you navigate?
questions.explication: With hash routing, only the fragment after `#` changes, so the browser does not request a new page from the server.

questions.question: Which statement about components is TRUE?
choix: They can only be used once per application
They must be written in TypeScript
They replace the need for a router
They encapsulate structure, logic and style
questions.explication: Components group HTML, JS and CSS into reusable, maintainable pieces.

questions.question: What is the minimum software a web server needs?
questions.explication: The software side of a web server comprises at least an HTTP server, which understands URLs and HTTP.

questions.question: A dynamic web server is a static web server plus…
choix: a CSS preprocessor and a CDN
a DNS server and a mail server
an application server and a database
a second HTTP server that keeps backups
questions.explication: Dynamic = static + application server + database, so pages can be generated from data.

questions.question: In the client-server sequence, what does the DNS server return?
choix: The HTML files of the website
The IP address of the web server
The CSS of the requested page
questions.explication: The browser asks DNS to translate the domain name into the web server's IP address, then sends its HTTP request to that IP.

questions.question: Which is listed as a DISADVANTAGE of the client-server model?
choix: Data is spread across every client
Servers are exposed to Denial of Service attacks
Client and server capacity can never be changed separately
questions.explication: Disadvantages: viruses spread from the server, DoS attacks on servers, packets spoofed or modified in transit. Centralised data and possible recovery are advantages.

questions.question: What does HTTPS need to encrypt traffic?
questions.explication: HTTPS uses cryptographic keys, usually through an SSL or TLS certificate.

questions.question: Which data should NOT be sent with GET?
questions.explication: GET data appears in the URL, history and bookmarks, so it is unsuitable for sensitive data. Use POST.

questions.question: Which pages are best served by a dynamic web server?
choix: A CSS file shared by all pages
A PDF of last year's timetable
questions.explication: Dynamic servers fit frequently changing, personalised content: logins, forms, inquiries, shopping carts.

questions.question: In MVC, which part interacts with the database?
questions.explication: The Model stores data objects and business rules and talks to the database.

questions.question: In the course's MVC view of a web app, which technology plays the Controller?
questions.explication: User interacts with the View (Vue.js), the Controller (Node.js) processes input and modifies data in the database (MySQL).

questions.question: Which ways does JavaScript offer to write asynchronous code?
choix: Classes, IDs, types and inline styles
questions.explication: The course lists callbacks, promises and async/await.

questions.question: Why is asynchronous code vital in JavaScript?
choix: JS is single-threaded, so waiting would block everything
Async code always runs faster than the same synchronous code
JS cannot run two lines of code in a row
questions.explication: With one thread, a blocking wait (network, timer) would freeze the page; async lets other code run meanwhile.

questions.question: Which statement describes Vue's reactive data?
choix: Vue copies the data into localStorage
Vue tracks data changes and updates the DOM
Data can only change when the page reloads
You must call render() after each change
questions.explication: Reactivity = Vue automatically tracks changes in data and re-renders the parts of the DOM that depend on them.

questions.question: `methods: { updateAge(n) { this.user.age = n; } }` is called. What happens to `{{ user.age }}`?
choix: It updates after a page reload
It stays the same until mount() is called
It throws an error, user is read-only
questions.explication: `user` is returned by data(), so it is reactive: changing `user.age` updates the template.

questions.question: In the MVVM view of Vue, what is the ViewModel?
choix: The HTML template of the page
The Vue instance linking View and Model
The CSS applied to the components
The database that stores the application data
questions.explication: View = UI, Model = data, ViewModel = the Vue instance that binds them reactively.

questions.question: In Vue 3, what does `ref('Hello')` return in `<script setup>`?
choix: A route reference for Vue Router
A reactive reference to the value
A plain string that cannot change
A link to a DOM element by id
questions.explication: `ref()` creates a reactive value usable in the template, e.g. `const message = ref('Hello from Vue 3!')`.

questions.question: How do you load Vue 3 in a simple HTML page, as in the course examples?
choix: With a `<link>` tag in the head
With `import Vue` in the HTML body
With a `<script>` tag pointing to a CDN
questions.explication: The course uses `<script src="https://unpkg.com/vue@3"></script>` (or jsdelivr), then `const { createApp } = Vue;`.

questions.question: Why is `computed` better than a method for `reversedMessage`?
choix: It is reactive derived state, recalculated when message changes
It runs only once when the app starts
It is the only option allowed to read data
It can be called with arguments directly from the template
questions.explication: Computed properties are derived state that Vue keeps in sync with their dependencies.

questions.question: In Vue 2, `this.newProp = 'x'` works on a property declared in data(). What fails to be reactive?
choix: A property that did not exist in data() at creation
A property declared with an empty string
Any property changed from inside a method of the instance
questions.explication: Vue 2 makes reactive only the properties present when the instance is created; new ones need `Vue.set()`.

questions.question: In a Vue method, how do you read the `message` data property?
questions.explication: Inside the options (methods, computed), data properties are available on `this`.

questions.question: What does `.mount('#app')` do in Vue 3?
choix: Loads the file app.vue from the server before rendering
Attaches the app to the element with id app
Creates a new element with id app
questions.explication: mount() connects the app to an existing DOM element, the equivalent of `el: '#app'` in Vue 2.

questions.question: `<button v-on:click="count++">` — what happens on click?
choix: Nothing, v-on needs a method name
questions.explication: v-on accepts a method name or a short inline expression like `count++`.

questions.question: Which directive should you use to show a block only when `isLoggedIn` is true?
questions.explication: v-if renders the element only when its condition is truthy.

questions.question:
`items: ['a','b','c']` and `
  • {{ item }}
    • `. How many `
  • ` are rendered?
questions.explication: v-for creates one element per array entry.

questions.question: After `this.items.push({ id: 4, name: 'Item 4' })` in the course's v-for example, what happens?
choix: Nothing until the page is refreshed
The list is replaced by Item 4 only
An error: push is not reactive
questions.explication: Array methods like push are tracked by Vue: the list re-renders with the new item.

questions.question: Which directive binds the `href` of a link to the data property `url`?
questions.explication: Attributes are bound with v-bind (`:`).

questions.question: What is wrong with `` in Vue?
choix: imageSource must be declared in methods, not in data
The img tag cannot be used inside #app
Mustaches do not work inside attributes; use `:src`
questions.explication: `{{ }}` only works in text content. For attributes, use `v-bind:src` or `:src`.
questions.piege: This is a classic debugging question.

questions.question: What does `v-model` keep in sync?
choix: The CSS and the HTML of an element
A component and its parent route
A form input and a data property
questions.explication: v-model creates two-way binding between a form input and data.

questions.question:
`

` with `htmlContent: '

Updated

'`. What appears?
questions.explication: v-html inserts the string as real HTML.

questions.question: Which directive repeats an element for each element of a list?
questions.explication: v-for iterates over an array or object.

questions.question: What does `:key` need to be in a v-for list?
choix: The index of the parent component
questions.explication: Each key must be unique so Vue can identify and track each element.

questions.question: `isVisible: false`, `isLoading: false`. What does the course's v-if / v-else-if / v-else block show?
questions.explication: Both conditions are false, so the v-else block is rendered.

questions.question:
`

Hello

` with `message: 'Hi'`. What is displayed?
questions.explication: v-text replaces the whole text content of the element with the value of the expression.

questions.question:
What does `` + `

{{ name }}

` do when the user types "Ana"?
choix: The paragraph shows Ana after a reload
The paragraph shows Ana while typing
The input is cleared after each key
questions.explication: v-model updates `name` on each input event, and the paragraph is reactive.

questions.question: What is a Vue component, according to the course?
choix: A reusable Vue instance with a name
A database table used by Vue
A route defined in the Express server
A CSS file attached to a page
questions.explication: Components are reusable Vue instances with a name, e.g. `my-component`.

questions.question: In Vue 2, how is a global component registered?
questions.explication: Vue 2: `Vue.component()`. Vue 3: `app.component()` on the app created by createApp.

questions.question: In the child, which line declares a prop named `title`?
questions.explication: Props are declared with the `props` option (array of names in the course).

questions.question: In the parent, which listener receives `this.$emit('updateMessage', msg)` from the child?
questions.explication: Custom events are listened to like native ones, with `@` (v-on).

questions.question: What is the second argument of `this.$emit('updateMessage', newMessage)`?
choix: The payload sent to the parent
The prop that will be overwritten
The delay before the event fires
The name of the parent component
questions.explication: The extra arguments are the data passed to the parent's handler, here `updateMessage(newMessage)`.

questions.question: Which three blocks can a `.vue` Single File Component contain?
questions.explication: An SFC groups `<template>`, `<script>` and `<style>` in one .vue file.

questions.question: In an SFC, what does `export default { ... }` in `<script>` contain?
choix: The CSS rules of the component
The list of routes of the app
The HTML template and the CSS of the component
questions.explication: The script block exports the component options object.

questions.question:
`

Hi

`, but the child template has no ``. What is shown?
choix: Hi, placed at the bottom of the child's template
Hi, placed at the top of the child
Only the child's own template; Hi is dropped
questions.explication: Content passed by the parent is rendered only where the child puts `<slot>`.

questions.question: In the course's custom-input, why use `:value` + `@input` instead of `v-model` on the inner input?
choix: v-model cannot be used inside templates
:value is faster than v-model when the input holds numbers
Props must not be modified directly by the child
questions.explication: The child receives `modelValue` as a prop; it shows it with `:value` and asks the parent to change it by emitting `update:modelValue`.

questions.question: Which Vue 3 file block sets up reactive state with less boilerplate?
questions.explication: `<script setup>` lets you declare `const message = ref(...)` directly.

questions.question: Which benefit do async components bring?
choix: Automatic HTTPS for the component and its children
questions.explication: They are downloaded only when needed, improving performance.

questions.question: Where is `my-component` registered in `createApp({ components: { 'async-component': AsyncComponent } })`?
choix: In Vue Router, as a route
Globally, for every Vue app on the page
Locally, for this app's root component
questions.explication: The `components` option registers components locally; `app.component()` registers them globally.

questions.question: The page shows `{{ message }}` literally instead of its value. What is the most likely cause?
choix: The Vue app is not mounted on that element
message is longer than 20 characters, so Vue skips it
questions.explication: If Vue is not loaded or `mount('#app')`/`el` does not match the element, the template is never compiled and the mustaches stay as text.

questions.question: `createApp({...}).mount('app')` — nothing renders. Why?
choix: createApp must be written new createApp
The data function must be async
mount() must be called before createApp
questions.explication: mount takes a CSS selector; an id is written `#app`.

questions.question: `<button @click="increment()">` and `methods: { increment: () => { this.count++; } }`. Nothing changes. Why?
choix: An arrow function does not get the Vue `this`
count must be declared in methods
questions.explication: Arrow functions do not have their own `this`, so `this.count` is not the component's data. Use `increment() { this.count++; }`.

questions.question: `<li v-for="item in itmes" :key="item.id">` shows an empty list although `items` has 3 entries. The bug?
choix: A typo: itmes instead of items
items must be declared in computed
v-for must be on the ul
questions.explication: Names in the template must match data exactly; `itmes` is undefined.

questions.question: The parent writes `<child @update-message="onUpdate">` and the child emits `this.$emit('updateMsg')`. The parent never reacts. Why?
choix: The event names do not match
onUpdate must be a computed property
The child must declare props first
questions.explication: The name emitted and the name listened to must be the same event.

questions.question:
`` and `

{{ name }}

`: typing does not update the paragraph. Fix?
questions.explication: v-bind is one-way (data → input). v-model is two-way.

questions.question: Vue 2: `addProperty() { this.$data.extra = 'x'; }`, `{{ extra }}` never updates. Fix?
choix: Move addProperty into computed so it is cached
questions.explication: Vue 2 cannot detect added properties; Vue.set makes them reactive (or declare `extra` in data from the start).

questions.question:
`
A
B
` gives a warning. What is wrong?
choix: The second div needs a key
v-if cannot use a single letter
questions.explication: v-else-if takes an expression (e.g. `v-else-if="b"`); only v-else has none.

questions.question: `<my-component :message="parentMessage">` but the parent's data is `{ parentMsg: 'Hi' }`. What does the child show?
questions.explication: parentMessage does not exist in the parent, so the prop receives undefined. Names must match.

questions.question: A Vue 3 custom input emits `this.$emit('input', e.target.value)` and is used with `v-model`. Typing does nothing. Fix?
choix: Register it with Vue.component instead of app.component
questions.explication: In Vue 3, v-model on a component listens to `update:modelValue`; `input` is the Vue 2 convention.

questions.question: `<button v-on:click="changeMessage">` but the method is defined in `data()` instead of `methods`. What happens?
choix: The button is hidden by Vue
It works exactly the same way
The click handler is not found as a method
The method runs once on page load, then never again
questions.explication: Functions meant as handlers belong in the `methods` option.

questions.question: Clicking adds items with `this.items.push({ id: 1, name: 'New' })` each time, and Vue warns about duplicate keys. Why?
choix: push is not reactive in Vue 3
Every new item has the same id used as :key
name must be unique instead of id for every pushed item
questions.explication: Keys must be unique; the course builds the id from `this.items.length + 1`.

questions.question: In a template, `{{ this.message }}` vs `{{ message }}`: which is the usual way?
questions.explication: In templates, data properties are used directly by name; `this` is used inside script options.

questions.question: A route `/profile/:id` works, but `userId: this.$route.params.Id` is always undefined. Why?
choix: $route is only available in main.js, not in components
questions.explication: The parameter is named exactly as in the path: `:id` → `params.id`.

questions.question: The SFC has `<style scoped>div { color: blue; }</style>`; a div in ANOTHER component is not blue. Is this a bug?
choix: No, scoped styles apply only to this component
Yes, scoped must be removed when using Vue 3 components
No, divs can never be styled in Vue
questions.explication: That is the purpose of `scoped`.

questions.question: What does Vue Router enable?
choix: Sending SQL queries directly from the browser
questions.explication: Vue Router maps URLs to components for client-side navigation.

questions.question: Which line installs the router plugin in a Vue 2 app?
questions.explication: `Vue.use(VueRouter)` registers the plugin before creating `new VueRouter({ routes })`.

questions.question: In `{ path: '/user/:id', component: User }`, what is `:id`?
questions.explication: `:id` matches any value in that position, e.g. /user/42 → params.id = '42'.

questions.question: How is the router given to the root instance in the course's main.js?
questions.explication: The router object is passed as an option of the root instance, which is then mounted with `.$mount('#app')`.

questions.question: Which element creates a navigation link handled by Vue Router?
questions.explication: `<router-link>` navigates; `<router-view>` displays the matched component.

questions.question: Where is `<router-view>` usually placed?
choix: In every route component of the app
questions.explication: App.vue contains `<router-view>`, the slot where routed components appear.

questions.question: What does `this.$router.push('/about')` do?
choix: Sends a POST request to the /about page
Adds a new route named about
questions.explication: push changes the current route programmatically.

questions.question: Which command creates a package.json with default values?
questions.explication: `npm init -y` initialises a project and accepts all defaults.

questions.question: What does `res.send('Hello World')` do?
choix: Renders a Pug view named Hello World
Redirects to the Hello World page
Sends that text as the HTTP response
Logs the text in the server console
questions.explication: res.send sends a response body to the client.

questions.question: In an Express route handler `(req, res) => {...}`, what is `req`?
choix: An object used to build and send the response
The port the server listens on
A function that renders a template
An object with the incoming request's data
questions.explication: req = request: headers, URL parameters, query string, body… res = response: used to set the status and send HTML or JSON back.

questions.question: What does `res.render('about')` do?
choix: Reads the about field from the submitted form
Renders views/about.pug and sends the HTML
questions.explication: res.render uses the view engine to generate HTML from a template and sends it to the client.

questions.question: Why do you call `parseFloat(req.body.price)` before doing arithmetic?
choix: parseFloat rounds the price to an integer
It checks the field is required
It converts the price into another currency
questions.explication: Everything a form sends arrives as a string; `'10' + 5` gives `'105'`. parseFloat turns the text into a number first.

questions.question: In `const { name, email } = req.body;`, what is this syntax?
questions.explication: Destructuring extracts properties of an object into variables with the same names.

questions.question: A middleware must store a value that every rendered Pug view can read. Where does it put it?
questions.explication: Properties set on `res.locals` (e.g. `res.locals.user = 'Ana'`) are available in any view rendered for that request — a common middleware pattern.

questions.question: Which route handles `<form action="/register" method="post">`?
questions.explication: The Express method must match the form's method (POST) and its action path.

questions.question: What does `res.redirect('/list')` do at the end of a POST route?
choix: Deletes the form data from req.body
Tells the browser to go to /list
questions.explication: Redirect tells the browser to request another URL (here a GET on /list), which then shows the updated data. This avoids re-submitting the form on refresh.

questions.question: Which Node feature lets one thread handle many connections?
questions.explication: Node is single-threaded and uses an event loop with non-blocking I/O.

questions.question: Which is NOT a feature of Express listed in the course?
questions.explication: Two-way data binding is a front-end feature (Vue, Angular).

questions.question: Without `app.use(express.static('public'))`, a request to `/style.css` returns 404. Why?
choix: Express serves no files unless told to
CSS files must be in views
Pug cannot link to CSS files
The browser blocks CSS on localhost
questions.explication: Static files are only served by the static middleware, from the folder you name.

questions.question: How does Pug show that an element is nested inside another?
questions.explication: Pug has no closing tags; nesting comes from indentation.

questions.question: Which Pug line produces `<div class="box">`?
questions.explication: `.className` creates a div with that class (`div.box` also works). `#id` creates a div with an id.

questions.question: Which Pug line produces `<div id="main">`?
questions.explication: `#IDname` gives an id.

questions.question: How are attributes written in Pug?
questions.explication: Attributes go in parentheses, separated by commas: `input(type="number", name="age", required)`.

questions.question: What does the Pug line `li: a(href='/about') About` produce?
questions.explication: The colon is block expansion: it nests the next tag inside on the same line.

questions.question: Which Pug line writes the HTML5 doctype?
questions.explication: `doctype html` outputs `<!DOCTYPE html>`.

questions.question: In a Pug view, what does `if result` followed by an indented `p Result: #{result}` do?
choix: Shows the paragraph only once a result exists
Always shows Result: undefined, even before submitting
Sends the result to the server
questions.explication: The paragraph is rendered only when `result` was passed and is truthy, e.g. after the form was processed.

questions.question: In Pug, what does `a(href='mailto:' + user.email) #{user.email}` produce?
choix: A link to a page named mailto on the same site
An email link showing the user's email
A form that sends an email
questions.explication: Attribute values are JavaScript expressions, so they can be concatenated; `#{}` prints the address as link text.

questions.question: The route calls `res.render('list', { users: rows })`. In list.pug, what does `each user in users` loop over?
choix: The rows written inside the list.pug file
questions.explication: Variables passed in the object of res.render are available in the template; `each` iterates over the array.

questions.question: A Pug page that reuses a shared layout starts with…
questions.explication: `extends layout` reuses layout.pug; the page then fills the layout's `block content`.

questions.question: In the layout, what is `block content`?
choix: A comment ignored by Pug when it compiles the page
A loop over all the pages
A div with the class content
A placeholder that child templates fill
questions.explication: Blocks are named slots in a layout, redefined by templates that extend it.

questions.question: What is the difference between `h1= message` and `h1 message`?
choix: The second is invalid Pug syntax
The first prints the variable, the second the word
Both print the value of the variable
The first is a comment, the second a tag holding the value
questions.explication: `=` evaluates the expression; without it, the text after the tag is plain text.

questions.question: Which feature does Pug provide for security?
choix: It hides the source code from the browser
questions.explication: Values printed with `=` or `#{}` are HTML-escaped by default.

questions.question: Pug was originally called…
questions.explication: Pug was renamed from Jade because of a trademark.

questions.question: What does the `-g` flag mean in `npm install -g <package>`?
questions.explication: `-g` installs the package for the whole system, not just the current app.

questions.question: How do you run a script named `dev` declared in the `scripts` of package.json?
questions.explication: Custom scripts run with `npm run <scriptname>` (`npm start` is a shortcut for start).

questions.question: Why keep the front-end (client) and the back-end (server) in separate folders or projects?
choix: Vue cannot read files outside its folder
Separation of concerns between front-end and back-end
Express forbids JavaScript files in the root of a project
Each folder needs its own database
questions.explication: Separation of concerns: each part has one job, can be developed and scaled independently, and the front-end build can be served by the back-end.

questions.question: What is the DOM?
choix: A JavaScript library used to animate pages
A server program that stores the HTML files
A CSS file that lists the style of every element
A tree of the page's nodes that JavaScript can change
questions.explication: The Document Object Model represents the page as a tree of nodes (elements, attributes, text). JS — and Vue — update the page by changing this tree.

questions.question: What is an advantage of `addEventListener` over the `onclick` HTML attribute?
choix: It fires before the page has loaded
Several listeners can be attached to one element
It works without any JavaScript file
questions.explication: addEventListener keeps JS out of the HTML and lets you add several handlers for the same event.

questions.question:
Which selector targets `

` by its class?
questions.explication: `.` = class, `#` = id, bare name = tag type.

questions.question: What does `document.getElementById('header').innerHTML = 'New';` do?
choix: Creates a new element with the id header
Adds the class New to the header element
Changes the colour of the header to New
Replaces the content of the element with id header
questions.explication: innerHTML is a property: setting it replaces the element's content.

questions.question: What does "declarative rendering" mean in Vue?
choix: You declare every route in the Express server
You describe the UI from the data and Vue updates the DOM
You must declare all CSS rules inside the template
You write each DOM change by hand after every update
questions.explication: You write `{{ message }}`; Vue takes care of keeping the DOM in sync when `message` changes.

questions.question: `data() { message: 'Hi' }` — `{{ message }}` shows nothing. Why?
choix: data must be declared after methods
Strings cannot be stored in data()
message must be written in double quotes
questions.explication: data() must RETURN the object. Without `return`, the braces are just a block and data is undefined.

questions.question:
`items: []` and `

You have items

`. Is the paragraph rendered?
questions.explication: items.length is 0, which is falsy, so v-if does not render the element.

questions.question:
What does `` with `

Hi

` do?
choix: The button disappears after one click
Each click hides or shows the paragraph
The paragraph is shown only once
questions.explication: The inline expression flips the boolean; v-if reacts to each change.

questions.question: Two `<counter>` components each have `data() { return { count: 0 }; }`. Clicking the first one…
questions.explication: Because data is a function, each instance gets its own copy of the state.

questions.question: A child wants to change a value it received as a prop. What is the right approach?
choix: Emit an event so the parent updates its data
Declare the prop a second time in data()
Assign the new value to the prop directly
Use v-html to overwrite the prop
questions.explication: Data flows down through props and changes flow up through events: the parent owns the data and updates it.

questions.question: How does `<router-link to="/about">` differ from `<a href="/about">` in an SPA?
choix: It sends a POST request to the server
It changes the view without reloading the page
It only works for external websites
It opens the page in a new browser tab
questions.explication: router-link lets Vue Router swap the component client-side; a normal link reloads the whole page from the server.

questions.question: A route sends `res.send('OK')` and does not call next(). A logging middleware is declared AFTER it with `app.use`. Does it run for that request?
choix: No, app.use only runs on errors
No, the response was already sent
Yes, but only for POST requests
questions.explication: Express runs handlers in the order they are declared; once a route answers without calling next(), the chain stops. Order matters.

questions.question: For the URL `/search?q=vue`, where does Express put `q`?
questions.explication: Query string → req.query; path parameters (:id) → req.params; POST form data → req.body.

questions.question: What does `res.status(404).send('Not found')` tell the browser?
choix: The user must log in first
The requested resource does not exist
The request succeeded with no data
questions.explication: 404 = Not Found. 500 = server error (used in the error-handling middleware), 200 = OK.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is meant to remove a resource?
questions.explication: Express maps them to app.get, app.post, app.put, app.delete. PUT updates, DELETE removes.

questions.question: In `async function load() { const r = await fetch(url); }`, what does `await` do?
choix: Pauses load() until the result arrives, without blocking the page
Blocks the whole browser until the server answers
Turns fetch into a synchronous function forever
Sends the request again if it failed
questions.explication: await suspends only the async function; the rest of the page keeps running. This is the async/await style of asynchronous code.

questions.question: What does the Pug line `p.intro Hello` produce?
questions.explication: A tag followed by `.name` gets that class; `#name` would give an id.

questions.question: What does `input(type='text', name='q', required)` produce?
questions.explication: Attributes go in parentheses, separated by commas; a boolean attribute is written alone.

questions.question: In an app built with Vue and Express, which part renders the interface in the browser?
questions.explication: Vue is the client-side View; Express handles requests and data on the server (the Controller role in the course's MVC picture).

questions.question: Which option should hold a function called when a button is clicked?
questions.explication: Event handlers are methods. computed is for derived values, data for state, el for mounting.
